## Verdict
REVISE — restart-persistent attempt bounds and explicit control/history scheduling are needed for a trustworthy comparison.

## Critical gaps
- Attempt and ACK counters are not explicitly restart-persistent. Authorize/count attempts before emission, including partial transmissions, and preserve those counters across restart and commit failure; otherwise the stated bounds can reset while credits remain durable.

## Important improvements
- Separate forwarding eligibility from control eligibility. Inactive donors must retry reserved grants, and inactive receivers must send pending custody ACKs, without allowing retained payloads to make new recipient deliveries. Legacy `_hello_round`/`_round` eligibility is forwarding-gated and cannot be reused unchanged.
- Define the HELLO/history epoch and common resource-arbitration order. Own and advertised scores must represent comparable instants; current-round history updates must not depend accidentally on contact enumeration.
- For a controlled clustered-versus-scattered contrast, reuse the movement/availability realization and source identities, changing interests only—not merely using the same motion model.
- Declare the complete policy/copy-budget matrix before execution. Host-budget failures must remain visible and must not silently remove difficult rows from comparative rankings; use per-policy subprocess limits or invalidate the incomplete matched case.

## Validation gaps
- Restart repeatedly around attempt authorization and partial emission; verify DATA, ACK and total-egress limits cannot reset.
- After a last-credit reservation, verify retained bodies cannot initiate unrelated deliveries while original-grant retries remain possible.
- Permute contact enumeration under the declared scheduler and verify history advertisements and decisions retain the specified causal semantics.
